title: ITSector lost the Portuguese top spot to the same OutSystems slot logic as IG&H
content:
ITSector was the number-one Portuguese lead and is now priority 9. The recorded rationale is a pointer rather than an argument: same logic as IG&H. That logic is slot occupancy — an OutSystems practice means the app layer a Powerhouse engagement would sit in is already held by a proprietary competitor, so the firm has no gap to fill and a practice to defend.

At 600-plus staff ITSector is also past the size band the screen prefers for a first design partner, but size is not what the note leans on. The pointer to IG&H is the whole justification, which means the two rows stand or fall together: if the slot-occupancy criterion were ever revised, both demotions would need revisiting at once.

Recording the shared rationale explicitly matters because it makes the ranking auditable. Two of the strongest national picks were removed by one rule, not by two independent judgements, and that concentration is a fact about the screen rather than about either firm.
